programs.title: Dolphins Up Close with Bertie Gregory
programs.desc: British filmmaker Bertie Gregory brings nature's wonders to life with groundbreaking cinematography in some of Earth's most extreme environments.Recently, for example, National Geographic viewers could observe the inhabitants of the frosty south in the film "The Secret Life of Penguins".The heroes of the latest documentary are mammals famous for their intelligence.Equipped with drones, state-of-the-art cameras and underwater technologies, creators can capture their world from a previously unavailable perspective.A haven for marine mammals, the Azores are an archipelago of volcanic islands located in the central part of the Atlantic Ocean.They are considered one of the best places for observing whales and dolphins.Bertie Gregory reaches the coast of Portugal, where the hunting season is in progress.Thousands of predators hunt together for large schools of fish that form balls.The team, struggling with storms, tries to film this rare spectacle of nature.It also follows pods of dolphins that perform acrobatics by jumping out of the water.During his journey, Bertie also discovers the dark history of marine exploitation in the region.He has the opportunity to see the consequences of the whaling ban in the 1980s.

programs.title: Animal Fight Club
programs.desc: There is a constant struggle in the animal kingdom.Lions, elephants, polar bears and cobras engage in deadly fights.The cameras capture scenes full of tension, drama and determination.Each fight has a story behind it.An alligator boldly wanting to assert its dominance, a hungry bear fighting for food, or a fox taking part in a mating ritual - they will show their capabilities.Unique recordings show the colorful and cruel world of animals.Tactics, hidden weapons, deception - wild creatures use all possibilities and will stop at nothing to survive.

programs.title: Wild Hawaii
programs.desc: Hawaii was formed seven million years ago when it emerged from the sea.Initially, it was a volcanic wasteland, now it is considered an earthly paradise.Such a change is contrary to the laws of nature, and yet Hawaii is a wild Arcadia that is constantly transformed and influenced by numerous influences.Thanks to factors such as separation from the mainland, differences in altitude and tropical climate, the islands have developed an extremely rich flora and fauna, including species threatened with extinction;in fact, there are most of them here.
